rows.text: Information from the meeting of the Monetary Policy Council
The Council decided to keep the NBP interest rates unchanged:
Incoming data signal that the annual GDP growth in the euro area in 2025 Q1 was probably similar as in 2024 Q4.
At the same time, inflation in this economy declined slightly and runs close to the central bank's target, whereas core inflation is still elevated.
Meanwhile, the United States saw signs of some weakening of economic conditions, amidst inflation remaining somewhat above the central bank's target.
The outlook for economic activity and inflation around the world is fraught with uncertainty, which is
In Poland, available data indicate that economic activity growth in 2025 Q1 was probably lower than expected and close to the 2024 Q4 figure.
In February annual growth rates of retail sales and of industrial output were negative, while growth of construction and assembly production declined.
In the labour market unemployment remains low and the number of working persons continues to be high, although employment in the enterprise sector in February 2025 was lower than a year earlier.
Wage growth is still running at the high level, but data from the enterprise sector point to lowering of wage growth.

Considering revised Statistics Poland data on consumer prices growth rates at the beginning of 2025 together with flash estimate for March 2025, annual CPI inflation in 2025 Q1 was lower than expected and stood at 4.9%.

In the Council's assessment, in the coming months inflation will remain above the NBP inflation target, driven by the effects of the already introduced increases in energy prices, as well as by the rises in excise duties and administered services prices.
Core inflation will be a further rise in regulated energy prices.

The Council judges that the current level of the NBP interest rates is conducive to meeting the NBP inflation target in the medium term.
